didYouKnow: Obesity prevalence has more than quadrupled since 1990 — from ~231 million to 878 million adults.
No country has successfully reversed its obesity epidemic at the population level.
1 in 7 adults worldwide were living with obesity in 2024.
Childhood obesity rates are rising fastest in low- and middle-income countries.

faq.q: How many people are obese worldwide?
faq.a: As of 2022-2024, approximately 878 million adults and 159 million children and adolescents were living with obesity globally (BMI ≥ 30 for adults).

faq.q: Which country has the highest obesity rate?
faq.a: Pacific island nations like Nauru and American Samoa have the highest rates (>55%). Among larger nations, the United States has one of the highest rates at ~42.4%.
Obesity continues to increase globally. Adult obesity prevalence has more than quadrupled since 1990, with no country achieving population-level reversal.

faq.q: What is the economic cost of obesity?
faq.a: Obesity-related healthcare and productivity costs exceed $2 trillion annually. The World Obesity Federation projects $4.3 trillion by 2060 if current trends continue.

faq.q: How does childhood obesity compare to adults?
faq.a: 159 million children and adolescents (5-19 years) were living with obesity in 2022, with rates rising fastest in Africa and Asia.
